items.title: Eddie Marshall interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002
items.q: he was into Teddy Wilson... I was into bebop music when I was a teenager... I’m hearing these guys say, “Man he’s really a good piano player but you know, that’s that old fashioned shit, I like bebop.”

ctx.x: Right. There was a structure there.

So that concerns me. And not that I don’t appreciate the youth in America. You know a lot of it is age too. I mean sometimes I sound like my dad. Because I grew up living with, you know my family is very, very musical. And my dad plays and my mom played the piano, everybody played the piano. And he was into Teddy Wilson, and Art Tatum, Nat King Cole, who I love too. But I was into bebop music when I was a teenager. I loved bebop music. And I’ll never forget that I was watching my father and we went to a party and…
I think some things never change.
